Jordanian Bank Workers Stage Nationwide Strike, Disrupting Branch Operations

Amman – Banking operations across Jordan have been severely disrupted since Tuesday as thousands of employees staged a coordinated walkout over stalled wage negotiations, causing widespread closure of bank branches and delays in processing within the country’s financial institutions.

The strike, organized by the Jordanian Bank Workers’ Union (JBWU), began after talks with the Jordanian Association of Banks (JAB) failed to yield agreement on salary adjustments and improved benefits. According to the union, over 80% of bank employees nationwide have participated, affecting both local and international banks operating in the Kingdom.

Large crowds of bank staff were seen picketing outside the Amman headquarters of Capital Jordan Bank and Al-Masaref National Bank, two of the country’s largest lenders. Many branches in central Amman, Irbid, Zarqa, and Aqaba remained shuttered, with signs posted informing customers of temporary closures. Automated teller machines operated by the banks continued to function, but in-branch services such as cash deposits, withdrawals over the counter, and document processing have been suspended in most locations.

“We have not taken this decision lightly,” said Saeed Al-Azazi, president of the JBWU. “After months of dialogue with bank management, our members felt their concerns were not being addressed. Our demand for a fair cost-of-living adjustment is long overdue.”

The walkout has also led to substantial backlogs in check clearing and loan application processing. Several institutions, including the Jordan Finance Bank Group, reported delays in approving new loans and mortgage applications due to the absence of key staff.

A senior official at Amman Commerce Bank, who asked not to be named, stated, “We are doing our best to maintain essential services, but the impact on daily operations is significant. Our human resources teams are in close discussions with the union to find a solution as soon as possible.”

Analysts say the strike could have lasting implications for employee relations and operational continuity in the sector. “This is an unprecedented action for Jordan’s banking industry,” said Lina Qasem, a financial sector analyst based in Amman. “The strike highlights underlying tensions over wages and working conditions that have been simmering for some time.”

As of Wednesday afternoon, negotiations had resumed between union representatives and the JAB. Both sides have expressed hope for “meaningful progress,” but no agreement had been reached at the time of writing. The union has stated that the strike will continue until a satisfactory resolution is achieved.
